title: Symmetry and periodicity

match.reason: No bank point teaches the symmetry and periodicity relationships between quadrants; the graphs point covers periods and asymptotes, and the unit circle point covers coordinates and quadrant signs, so both are related but different ideas.

draft.title: Symmetry and periodicity
card: Sine and cosine repeat every 2π, so sin(θ + 2π) = sin θ and cos(θ + 2π) = cos θ. Tangent repeats every π, so tan(θ + π) = tan θ.
Reflecting an angle in the y-axis gives π − θ: sin(π − θ) = sin θ and cos(π − θ) = −cos θ.
Going half a turn round gives π + θ: sin(π + θ) = −sin θ and cos(π + θ) = −cos θ. Reflecting in the x-axis gives −θ or 2π − θ: sin(−θ) = −sin θ and cos(−θ) = cos θ.
Worked example: sin(5π/6) = sin(π − π/6) = sin(π/6) = 1/2. The angle 5π/6 is in quadrant 2, where sine is positive.
draft.remember: Find the matching angle in quadrant 1, then fix the sign using the quadrant.

a.q: Which expression is equal to cos(π − θ)?
a.why: Reflecting in the y-axis keeps the height but flips the x-coordinate, so cosine changes sign: cos(π − θ) = −cos θ. The option cos θ is tempting, but that is the rule for sine, which keeps its sign.
a.clue: Reflecting in the y-axis changes the x-coordinate.

b.q: What is the value of cos(4π/3)?
b.why: 4π/3 = π + π/3, which is in quadrant 3, where cosine is negative. So cos(4π/3) = −cos(π/3) = −1/2. The option −√3/2 is tempting, but it is the value of sin(4π/3) and cos(7π/6), not of cos(4π/3).
b.clue: Write 4π/3 as π + π/3, then check the quadrant.
